THE PLAYGROUND

Welcome to the Playground.

The fourth room of the school, beside the Library, the School Garden and the Music Room: the action words our bodies do here, the things standing on the ground and the five manners that make play kind — the word cards sit on this page with their printable twins in the library, and the games shelf at the foot of the room holds twelve playground classics with their full rules.

THE ACTION WORDS

Fifteen words our bodies do at the playground.

Balance on the bench edge, catch the big ball, dig to the middle of the earth, run everywhere: every action word gets its own card, and every card is a game the body already wants to play. Every word’s lesson is right here — what it means, how the body does it and how to practise tonight.

BalanceCatchClimbDigHideJumpKickPlayPullPushRunSitSlideSwingWalk
ON THE GROUND

Twelve things you meet at the playground.

The ball that never says no, the slide that waits at the top, the sandbox with a square of beach inside it: the playground’s own furniture, one card and one lesson each. Name the place before you go and the trip gets a whole vocabulary louder.

BallBenchClimbing FrameFenceLadderMonkey BarsSandboxSeesawPlayground SlideSpring RiderPlayground SwingTunnel
HOW WE PLAY TOGETHER

Five manners that make the playground kind.

Help, share, stop, take turns, wait — the five words that turn a playground full of wanters into a playground full of friends. Each card comes with its lesson right here: the word, the words to say and one way to practise it before you even get there.

HelpShareStopTake TurnsWait
GAMES WE PLAY HERE

Twelve games this playground was built for.

The circle forms for Duck Duck Goose, the chalk slab becomes a hopscotch court, and the open grass is a Red Light Green Light lane the moment somebody shouts green. Each card opens its rules page on the school’s games shelf — the steps in order, the things to gather and a brand-new way to run the game tomorrow. The other twenty-three games, from Balloon Keep-Up to Treasure Hunt, wait on the games shelf too.

PLAY FAIR

The five manners meet thirty-two more.

The Playground keeps five manners cards — the ones play needs most. The Manners flashcards next door carry the full set: take turns and let-others-go-first for the slide queue, quiet voices and walking feet for the halls — thirty-two cards for ages 3–5 with a tip, a download and a print button on each, all on one page.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 32 cards in Playground, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Playground. We have 32 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Balance

    “Arms out, eyes forward — step… step… steady! Balance is your body talking to itself, and you are the boss of it.”

    How: Tape a line on the floor and walk it forwards, backwards and sideways. Then try it with a beanbag on your head and see how far Mr. Beanbag rides along.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Catch

    “Ready… watch the ball… now! Catch! Two hands close like a bird cage around the ball.”

    How: Start with a big, soft beach ball hugged against the chest. Step back one tiny step for every catch. Ten catches in a row earns a silly victory dance.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Climb

    “Hand, hand, foot, foot — up we go! Climb means your hands and feet are friends and they take turns.”

    How: Play “sticky hands” on the stairs at home: hands on the steps too — hands, feet, hands, feet, slowly, like a puppy. Same skill, indoors, zero height.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Dig

    “Scoop and sprinkle, scoop and sprinkle — dig, dig, dig! What will we find under the sand today?”

    How: Bury a treasure (a big spoon, a toy, a shiny stone) and dig it up again. Bury it deeper each time and listen to the effort grow.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Hide

    “One, two, three… where ARE you? Hide means quiet feet and a held breath and a grin you hope nobody sees.”

    How: Hide a toy instead of a person first. Hide it badly on purpose — a tail sticking out — and let your child gloat. Then let them hide it for you.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Jump

    “Bend your knees… wiggle… JUMP! Both feet up, both feet down, land like a cat with bendy knees.”

    How: Chalk two lines on the path and jump between them, then widen the river one shoe-length at a time. How wide can the crocodile river get before the jumping fails?

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Kick

    “Plant your foot next to the ball, swing the other one — WHACK! Kick means one leg says hello to the ball, hard.”

    How: Kick a balloon first — it hangs in the air long enough to feel successful. Then a soft ball, then a real one, and finally set up two shoes as a goal and shoot.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Play

    “Play is what we do when nobody is telling us what to do — running, pretending, building, giggling, again again again!”

    How: Ask “what are we playing?” and then join the game by its own rules — if the floor is lava, your feet are in terrible danger. Follow the leader your child appoints.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Pull

    “Lean back and heave — pull, pull, PULL! The wagon follows the person who pulls it, like a duckling on wheels.”

    How: Load a laundry basket with toys, tie a rope on and make it a train with stations. The passenger load decides whether the engine glides or groans.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Push

    “Hands on, bend your legs, PUSH! The roundabout only goes because someone pushes it — today that someone is you.”

    How: Push games indoors: push a box of books across the rug, push your grown-up (gently!), push the shopping trolley. Heavy things make honest pushes.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Run

    “Quick feet, elbows in — run, run, run! Running is walking that got exciting.”

    How: Play “red light, green light” or race to the tree and back. Short sprints with a finish line teach more than long chases — and the finish line is where the laughing happens.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Sit

    “Bottom down, legs crossed — sit! Sitting is how your body takes a drink of quiet.”

    How: Make the bench a shop, a bus or a pirate look-out. Sitting that has a story in it lasts twice as long as sitting that is just sitting.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Slide

    “Up the steps, sit, feet first — WHEEE! Slide means the playground does the moving and you do the laughing.”

    How: Slide counting: how many times can you slide before your legs get wobbly? Count out loud together — the number will be higher than you fear.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Swing

    “Lean back, legs out… tuck them in… swing! The legs are the engine and the sky is the destination.”

    How: Behind-push first, then teach pumping with a rhyme: “out like a frog, in like a mouse.” One rhyme, one pump, and one day the pushes stop being needed.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Walk

    “Heel, toe, heel, toe — walk! Walking is just falling forwards and catching yourself, over and over, on purpose.”

    How: Walk home the slow way and let your child lead. Every twenty steps they pick the next turn — the map goes silly, the walking never notices.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Ball

    “Round and ready — a ball never says no. Bounce it, roll it, kick it, hug it: the ball plays whatever game you bring.”

    How: Roll the ball back and forth sitting down, then bounce it standing, then kick it running. Same ball, three difficulties — your child picks the level.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Bench

    “The bench is waiting — sit, snack, chat, go again. It is the playground’s kitchen table with the best view.”

    How: Bench games: shopkeeper behind the counter, bus driver on the route, audience for the show. One bench, three careers.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Climbing Frame

    “Grab the bars, find your feet — the climbing frame is a mountain that waits for small climbers and claps when they cross.”

    How: Play “the floor is water” under the frame — feet stay on the bars. Then cross it three ways and pick a favourite route to show a friend.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Fence

    “The fence holds the playground like a hug — inside it, the running goes wild; outside it, the road does road things.”

    How: Fence games: touch-the-fence tag (the fence is base), “what colour is your post?”, and counting the posts on the walk out. The border becomes a landmark.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Ladder

    “One rung, two rung — hands and feet take turns. The ladder says: slow is fine, steady is better, the top is patient.”

    How: Chalk a ladder on the pavement and hop it — two feet in each space, then one. Same climbing rhythm, ground floor, no height.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Monkey Bars

    “Hand, hand, hand — swing across! The monkey bars ask your arms to be brave and your legs to just hang out.”

    How: Build a home version with a sturdy broom held between two grown-ups. Three bars of practice at home make the playground row feel familiar.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Sandbox

    “Shoes off (or not) — the sandbox is open! Scoop, pour, pat, repeat: the sand never says the game is over.”

    How: Bury a row of “gems” (bottle caps) and dig for treasure by number: “find four!” Scooping to an exact count is a sneaky maths lesson.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Seesaw

    “Up… and down… up… and down! The seesaw only works when both ends agree to play — light end up, heavy end down.”

    How: Two riders of very different weights? Move the small one closer to the middle — the magic balance point exists, and finding it is a real experiment.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Playground Slide

    “Up the blue ladder, quick sit, feet first — WHEEE, down the yellow! The slide is the playground’s promise: what goes up happily, comes down giggling.”

    How: Race a different way each turn: feet first, on a grown-up’s lap (for the smallest sliders), and — the crowd favourite — spot your house from the top.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Spring Rider

    “Hop on, hold the handles, bounce bounce bounce — the yellow horse rocks because YOU rock. Rock harder, ride wilder!”

    How: Rock to a song — fast for the fast part, slow for the slow part. The spring keeps perfect time, and the song keeps the bouncing from going full storm.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Playground Swing

    “Sit deep, hold tight, lean back — the swing moves when YOU move. Pump out like a frog, tuck in like a mouse.”

    How: Count the pumps: how many leg pumps to touch the leaves? Then try the quiet game — swing with no pushes at all, just rhythm, as long as you can.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Tunnel

    “Hands and knees, off we go — through the tunnel! It is dark in the middle and that is the fun part: round the bend, out the end.”

    How: Peek-a-boo with the tunnel: one crawls, one waits at the end and pops in — “THERE you are!” Then swap. It never stops being funny.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Help

    “Do you need a hand? Here — I’ll help! Helping makes the playground bigger: two people can lift what one person cannot.”

    How: Play “spot the helping chance” on the way home: someone dropped a mitten, a friend’s zipper is stuck, the gate needs holding. Every spot is a chance to practise.

  33. 30
    Card 29 · Share

    “You hold it, I hold it — we share! Sharing means the toy plays with BOTH of us, and the game gets twice as big.”

    How: Split a snack deliberately: “one for you, one for me.” Then let your child do the splitting for the family. Fairness is a skill the splitter learns fastest.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Stop

    “Hand up, feet freeze — STOP! Stop is the brakes. When someone says it, we all stop and look. Then we decide what happens next.”

    How: Play freeze games where STOP is the rule: dance until the song says stop, run until the whistle says stop. Practise the brake when nothing is wrong, so it works when something is.

  35. Cards 31–32
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Take Turns

    “My go… your go… my go! Turns are like a wave at the beach — it always comes back to you.”

    How: Use a turn-taking song or a counted turn: “ten pushes, then swap.” The count makes the end visible, and visible ends turn waiting from misery into anticipation.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Wait

    “My body waits, my eyes watch — it is almost my go! Waiting is not doing nothing; it is watching the game until my turn arrives.”

    How: Give waiting a job: count the pushes, name the colours that go by, guess how long (one hippo? two hippos?). A waiting brain with a task stops noticing the clock.

  38. 34
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  39. 35
    Check

    “Can you find Balance? Now show me Bench.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  40. 36
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 32 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
